                    ### Question
                    A 44-year-old female presents to her primary care physician complaining of fatigue. She reports a four-month history of increasing fatigue accompanied by occasional constipation. She also reports a 15-pound weight gain over the same time period. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. She has never been pregnant. On physical examination, her skin is dry and cracked. Patellar reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. Laboratory analysis reveals an elevated serum TSH and decreased serum and free T4. Her blood is positive for the presence of specific antibodies. A biopsy of this patient’s thyroid gland would most likely reveal which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Large pleomorphic cells with vascular invasion and necrosis
opb. Randomly oriented papillae with pleomorphic cells and dense fibrosis
opc. Spindle cells with stromal amyloid deposition
opd. Lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal center formation
ope. Hyperplasia and hypertrophy of follicular cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case, the most likely finding on biopsy of the patient's thyroid gland would be lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal center formation, consistent with autoimmune thyroid disease. The presence of specific antibodies supports the diagnosis of autoimmune thyroid disease, leading to this characteristic histological feature.
